headline: LA COLORADA RETURNS 22.1 g/t Au (1.3m VEIN AT 174 g/t) AS HELIOSTAR LOCKS IN VETA MADRE PLUS PIT PERMITS
snippet: Heliostar Metals Ltd. (TSXV: HSTR) announced June 18, 2026 a dual catalyst from its La Colorada gold mine in Sonora, Mexico — new drill results and simultaneous receipt of all permits required to advance the Veta Madre Plus open-pit cutback, targeting more than 20,000 additional ounces above the existing mine plan. Standout holes include 10.9 metres grading 22.1 g/t Au (including 1.3 metres at 174 g/t Au) and 40.8 metres at 2.23 g/t Au (including 17.45 metres at 4.55 g/t Au), alongside a bulk-tonnage 147.2-metre intercept at 0.70 g/t Au — all from a 44-hole, 8,425-metre campaign at the producing heap-leach operation. The CUS permit, environmental permits, and leach pad expansion approvals are all in hand, with Veta Madre Plus cutback scheduled to commence Q3 2026. For investors tracking Sonora gold producers through the current $4,155/oz gold market, a producing mine that simultaneously delivers 174 g/t Au vein grades in the same week it secures every permit required for its next expansion represents a compressed catalyst sequence that is rare even in active gold markets.

headline: N2 GOLD A-ZONE BREAKS WEST — FORMATION METALS DRILLS 1.75 g/t Au/30.4m IN UNTESTED QUÉBEC GROUND AHEAD OF Q3 MRE
snippet: Formation Metals Inc. (CSE: FOMO) reported June 18, 2026 drill results that extend the A-Zone at its N2 Gold Project in Québec 200 metres west of the historic resource boundary into previously undrilled ground — a structural step-out confirming open mineralization beyond the known footprint just weeks before a Q3 2026 maiden NI 43-101 Mineral Resource Estimate. Hole N2-26-021 returned 1.75 g/t Au over 30.4 metres and 0.91 g/t Au over 42.3 metres; N2-26-022 intersected 1.05 g/t Au over 31 metres — both holes exhibiting the same mineralization style as the A-Zone's known core, indicating a continuous system rather than a disconnected satellite. The company's 75,000-metre, fully funded 2026 drill program remains active, with the Q3 maiden MRE now targeting a larger footprint than the program commenced with. For investors assessing junior gold explorers in the current market — where a maiden resource estimate is the most consistent re-rating catalyst available — A-Zone step-outs delivered 200 metres into blank ground ahead of the MRE deadline add direct ounces to the estimate's upside envelope at a critical timing window.

headline: RUA GOLD DRILLS BEYOND 1,000m STRIKE AT AULD CREEK — NZ GOLD-ANTIMONY PFS AND FAST-TRACK PERMIT TARGETED Q4 2026
source_name: Newsfile / RUA GOLD Inc. (TSX: RUA; NZX: RGI; OTCQX: NZAUF)
snippet: RUA GOLD Inc. (TSX: RUA) announced June 18, 2026 drilling at the Auld Creek Gold-Antimony Project on New Zealand's South Island has now defined more than 1,000 metres of strike and 500 metres of depth — supporting an accelerated Pre-Feasibility Study and Fast-Track Mining Application both targeted for Q4 2026. The previously published PEA modelled a no-cyanide flowsheet delivering 84,000 ounces of gold plus 9,000 tonnes of antimony annually (approximately 27,000 AuEq oz/year additional), achieving 95% gold and 85% antimony recovery without any cyanide reagent. New Zealand's Fast-Track Approvals regime, enacted in 2025, provides an expedited permitting pathway for nationally significant mining projects — and Auld Creek's antimony production positions it directly within critical mineral supply chain frameworks given antimony's approximate 90% Chinese supply concentration and its designation as a critical mineral in Canada, the US, and the EU. A New Zealand gold-antimony project combining no-cyanide metallurgy, PFS-stage economics, and a Fast-Track regulatory pathway in a stable jurisdiction is one of the more distinctly positioned critical mineral stories available in the current market.

headline: AMERICAN RARE EARTHS DRILLS 5 DFS HOLES AT HALLECK CREEK — WYOMING REE COMPLEX AND THREE MORE U.S. PROJECTS ADVANCE
source_name: GlobeNewswire / American Rare Earths Ltd. (ASX: ARR; OTCQX: ARRNF)
snippet: American Rare Earths Ltd. (ASX: ARR) provided June 18, 2026 a portfolio update confirming that five of nineteen planned HQ core holes have been completed in the Cowboy State Mine area of its Halleck Creek rare earth project in Wyoming, advancing the dataset toward a Definitive Feasibility Study with assay turnaround expected at approximately six weeks. The company also outlined 2026-2027 field programs across La Paz (Arizona), Beaver Creek (Wyoming), and Searchlight (Nevada) — four entirely domestic US projects at various stages of resource and feasibility advancement. With the Pentagon's conditional US$725 million DoD loan to Energy Fuels confirmed this week and the Energy Fuels/ASM rare earth merger pending shareholder vote on June 22, the US government's active capital deployment into domestic REE infrastructure is accelerating — giving fully domestic REE developers like American Rare Earths a structurally improved financing and offtake environment as the US Commerce Department and DoD continue to de-risk the ex-China rare earth supply chain.

headline: THESIS GOLD 20,000m FS DRILL BEGINS AT LAWYERS-RANCH — C$1.28B NPV TOODOGGONE PROJECT TARGETS 2027 FEASIBILITY STUDY
source_name: PR Newswire / Thesis Gold & Silver Inc. (TSXV: TAU; OTCQX: THSGF)
snippet: Thesis Gold & Silver Inc. (TSXV: TAU) announced June 17, 2026 the commencement of its 2026 program at the Lawyers-Ranch Project in BC's Toodoggone Mining District — a 20,000-metre campaign split between 12,000 metres of exploration drilling targeting the Ranch and Ranch East zones and 8,000 metres of geotechnical, hydrogeological, and metallurgical drilling required for Feasibility Study inputs. The December 2025 Pre-Feasibility Study established a 15-year mine life, a 35.2% after-tax IRR, and a C$1.28 billion NPV5% — economics that position Lawyers-Ranch among the more compelling undeveloped gold-silver porphyry systems in northern BC, in a district that also includes district-scale exploration targets being evaluated simultaneously in this year's program. With a Feasibility Study targeted before end-2027, the 2026 drill program is the final major de-risking campaign before the project enters a financing-ready state. At gold near $4,155/oz — still historically exceptional economics for open-pit porphyry development — a BC gold-silver project with PFS-stage 35% IRR and a funded FS program in progress is one of the more advanced development stories on the Toodoggone.

headline: RECORD 45% OF CENTRAL BANKS PLAN TO BUY GOLD IN 12 MONTHS — WGC: BULLION NOW WORLD'S #1 RESERVE ASSET PAST US TREASURIES
source_name: Kitco News (WGC Central Bank Gold Reserves Survey 2026)
snippet: The World Gold Council's 2026 Central Bank Gold Reserves Survey — conducted across 76 reserve managers (record participation) and published June 16, 2026 — found that 45% of central banks plan to increase their own gold reserves over the next 12 months, a new record and up from 43% in the prior year's survey, while 89% expect global central bank gold holdings to increase in aggregate. The survey confirmed that gold has now surpassed US Treasury securities to become the world's largest global reserve asset — a structural shift driven by four consecutive years of central bank purchases averaging approximately 1,000 tonnes per year, more than double the approximately 500 tonnes per year averaged in the prior decade. The reserve managers cited geopolitical risk, US fiscal trajectory, and sanctions concerns as the primary drivers of allocation increases. For gold investors navigating the current 25% correction from January's $5,589 ATH, the WGC data establishes that sovereign demand — the most price-inelastic buyer class in the gold market — is structurally accelerating into the weakness, providing a durable demand floor that retail and institutional sentiment surveys cannot replicate.

headline: VICUÑA COPPER WINS ARGENTINA RIGI PEELP — BHP-LUNDIN $9.7B JV IS COUNTRY'S LARGEST EVER MINING PROJECT
snippet: Vicuña Corp. — the 50/50 joint venture between BHP and Lundin Mining holding the Josemaría and Filo del Sol copper-gold deposits in Argentina's San Juan Province — received June 16, 2026 approval of its Preliminary Evaluation of Environmental and Social Potential Impacts (PEELP) under Argentina's RIGI large investment framework, making Vicuña the first copper mining project in Argentina to achieve this regulatory milestone. The RIGI framework, enacted in 2024, provides 30-year fiscal and royalty stability for investments above US$200 million — and Vicuña's initial capital budget of US$9.7 billion (with potential to reach US$18 billion through mine life) is Argentina's largest single mining project in history. The project is projected to generate US$2.6 billion in annual exports and support 30,000 direct and indirect jobs, with the PEELP approval marking the critical regulatory gateway before environmental impact assessment and construction permitting advance. In a copper market pricing a 15% Section 232 tariff by June 30 and a structural supply deficit through the 2030s, a BHP-Lundin JV clearing its first major sovereign regulatory hurdle in a newly RIGI-stabilised jurisdiction is one of the most significant copper development milestones of 2026.

headline: CANAMERA EXPANDS TURVOLÂNDIA TO FOUR REE TARGETS SPANNING 7.4km — SOUTH ZONE ADDS IONIC CLAY DISCOVERY IN MINAS GERAIS
source_name: StockTitan / Canamera Energy Metals Corp. (CSE: EMET; OTCQB: EMETF)
snippet: Canamera Energy Metals Corp. (CSE: EMET) announced June 16, 2026 the identification of a fourth rare earth target — the South Target — at its Turvolândia Project in Minas Gerais, Brazil, extending the project's defined ionic clay REE system to a 7.4-kilometre corridor across four named zones: Cordis, Marita, Linda, and South. The South Target's surface sampling returned up to 1,748.9 ppm TREO including 702.2 ppm MREO+Y₂O₃ over 6 metres — grades in line with the deposit's other ionic clay REE zones and consistent with the leachable ionic clay adsorption style that accounts for the majority of global rare earth production outside hard-rock mineral deposits. Ionic clay REE projects — the same geological type as China's dominant Jiangxi and Fujian province operations — are of particular interest to investors and government offtakers seeking ex-China REE supply, because their clay-hosted REEs are amenable to low-energy, low-infrastructure heap-leach extraction processes that generate lower capex and faster development timelines than conventional hard-rock REE mines. A 7.4-kilometre ionic clay REE corridor in Minas Gerais, Brazil — in a geologically analogous setting to China's producing ionic clay provinces — represents one of the larger footprints for this deposit style currently being advanced in South America.
